column1: # Cases for hooks/guard-bash.sh — <expected-exit>TAB<command>[TAB<label>]
# 2 = must block, 0 = must allow. \n is decoded to a real newline.
# The must-ALLOW half is not optional. A guard with only block-cases certifies
# a regex that also eats `grep -rn pytest tests/`.
# --- bypass classes: every guard must survive these ---------------------------
# --- safety must stay quote-aware for NON-executors: these only CONTAIN the
# destructive text as quoted DATA (grep pattern, echo string, commit message,
# jq expression) — widening the safety anchors to see through quotes once
# regressed all six of these into false blocks. Regression tests for that.
# --- make-wrapped calls: a shell separator INSIDE a quoted make arg is text
# handed to make, not a command position in the agent's own shell — routing
# must not fire on it. Safety (rm/git checks) still scans raw text regardless.

quoted rm is still a real rm: safety must still block

column1: # --- executor payloads: the quoted arg of `sh -c` / `NAME=` is re-checked as a
# command in its own right (one level). The must-ALLOW half is what keeps the
# recursion honest — an executor merely CO-OCCURRING with quoted destructive
# text is not an execution of it, and an earlier "executor anywhere => scan raw"
# shape blocked all four of these.
